condition.narrative: Section I.A.1 of the Loan AgreementThe Borrower shall vest the overall responsibility for the implementation of the Project inMOE, and to this end, shall, through MOE:(a) No later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such other date asagreed by the Bank, appoint and thereafter maintain a Project coordinator under terms of reference described in the ProjectOperational Manual.(b) No later than three (3) months after the Effective Date, or such other date as agreed by the Bank,establish, and thereafter maintain throughout Project implementation, the Project Steering Committee with composition acceptable tothe Bank and defined in the Project Operational Manual.

Section I.B.1 of Schedule 2 to the Loan AgreementFor purposes of the provision of Primary School Grants under Part 2.1(e) of theProject, upon achievement of DLR#2.1 as described in Schedule 4 of the Loan Agreement, the Borrower, through MOE, shall, uponselection of an Eligible Primary School pursuant to the criteria and procedures established in the POM, enter into a standardagreement with the Eligible Primary School, under terms and conditions acceptable to the Bank (the Primary School GrantAgreement).

title.narrative: 1. Children enrolled in public preschools in targeted districts (disaggregated by gender and urban/rural areas)

comment.narrative: 9,429 is the total number of enrolled children in public preschools in targeted districts for school year : 2024 - 2025. Data disaggregated by gender and rural/urban: Number of enrolled girls: 4644 Number of enrolled boys: 4785

title.narrative: 3. Public preschool classrooms assessed using quality assurance mechanism

comment.narrative: The DLI related to the QA mechanism was successfully disbursed last year, subsequent efforts to build on this achievement specifically through the launch of a preschool assessment have faced significant setbacks. Despite substantial preparatory work by the Ministry of Education, including workshops, inspector mobilization, sampling, tool adaptation, and testing, the implementation was disrupted by an inspectors strike. This unforeseen interruption has impeded progress, and as a result, the indicator is not met.

title.narrative: 10. Primary school classrooms equipped with a reading corner

comment.narrative: The procurement of books (storybooks for preparatory and primary classes), dictionaries, and encyclopedias for the benefit of 3,000 primary schools was launched on December 26, 2024. The evaluation phase remains ongoing; however, the procurement may not be finalized due to the approaching closure of the project.

title.narrative: 2. Preschool classrooms that have received learning materials and small supplies

comment.narrative: School furniture and playgrounds have been delivered to 150 preschool classrooms. Gymnastics mats were delivered 2,500 preschool classrooms. This indicator is met and exceeded end target

title.narrative: 1. Preschool teachers who receive in-service training on the core professional development program for early childhood education developed by the Ministry of Education

comment.narrative: 2,310 preschool teachers ( 80% of total number of preschool teachers) have benefitted from a training in theatrical activities as part of CENAFOP's 2023 agreement (total of preschool teachers in 2022 is around 2877 based on Edunet) . Under its 2024 agreement, CENAFOP has developed two preschool-focused modules: preschool curriculum and specific approaches of preschool.

title.narrative: 9. Inspectors and pedagogical counselors trained on coaching techniques, disaggregated by gender

comment.narrative: The total number of trained inspectors has been previously measured through the total of enrollments (Number of inspectors trained per module cumulative since 2019). The data has been maintained due to ongoing strikes by the inspectors (who serve as trainers) and will be updated based on inspectors training structure (CIFFIP).

title.narrative: 5. Primary school directors and deputy directors who have participated in training on leadership and school management delivered by the MOE (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: The total number of trained directors has been previously measured through the total of enrollments (Number of directors trained per module cumulative since 2019). The data has been maintained due to ongoing strikes by the inspectors (who serve as trainers) and will be updated at the conclusion of the final training contract (30 November), which includes principals training.

title.narrative: 7. Primary school teachers who receive in-service training on the core professional development program delivered by the MOE (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: This indicator was previously calculated as the cumulative total of teacher enrollments across modules. After reviewing data with CENAFOP, 51,472 teachers have been trained since 2019 under PREFAT on pedagogy, teaching practices, and core subjects such as Mathematics, Science, and Languages. The trained group includes newly recruited, temporary, and tenured primary teachers. Training activities are still ongoing, with the current agreement scheduled to close on November 30. This indicator is met and has exceeded the end target and expected to increase slightly by the end of November.

title.narrative: 4. Preschool classrooms built in selected districts

comment.narrative: 94 preschool classrooms have been built under PREFAT and 100 preschool classrooms will be finalized by the end of the project.

title.narrative: Students benefiting from direct interventions to enhance learning

comment.narrative: Based on data shared by MoE/DGEPSI for 2024-2025, the total number of primary pupils is 1,184,438. Given that 72% of primary teachers have received trainings sunder PREFAT since 2019, we can estimate that approximately 72% of pupils i.e: 852,780 pupils have benefited from trained teachers (which is a direct intervention of PREFAT).

This indicator was previously calculated as the cumulative total of teacher enrollments across modules. After reviewing data with CENAFOP, 51,472 teachers have been trained since 2019 under PREFAT on pedagogy, teaching practices, and core subjects such as Mathematics, Science, and Languages. The trained group includes newly recruited, temporary, and tenured primary teachers. Training activities are still ongoing, with the current agreement scheduled to close on November 30. This indicator is met and has exceeded the end target and expected to increase slightly by the end of November.

title.narrative: 15. Primary teachers who have received training to develop their skills set for distance education teaching

comment.narrative: Same data maintained as in the latest ISR. In second semester 2020 the Ministry has introduced a number of MOOCs focused on ICT from which 400 teachers, pedagogical assistants and inspectors have benefitted. In 2021, CNTE trained 360 teachers, 425 inspectors and 133 pedagogical assistants on remote collaboration tools (Teams, OneDrive, Sharepoint, Azur Cloud). CNTE also developed a specific tool to ensure pedagogical continuity through virtual classrooms and trained 750 teachers and 150 inspectors. As part of CENAFOP's agreement 2023, 7330 teachers have benefitted form distance teaching module. The total number of teachers who have received training to develop their skills set for distance education teaching is 9,548.00.

title.narrative: Teachers who agree that professional development activities help them improve their classroom practices

comment.narrative: Same data maintained as in the latest ISR. CENAFOP surveyed the teachers benefitting from training modules during 2023 and 2024. Data communicated by CENAFOP Based on the results of the satisfaction surveys completed for PREFAT modules and communicated by CENAFOP, shows that 93.3% of teachers claim that presented content serve as a reliable reference in their professional work.
